en.title: New Streaming Arrivals: A Time-Traveling Ship, A Love Triangle, and More
en.summary: This week's streaming lineup offers a fascinating blend of genres, from a mysterious maritime adventure to an emotionally charged romantic drama. Dive into these fresh arrivals that promise to captivate audiences.
en.body:
Get ready to refresh your watchlist! A compelling collection of new titles has just docked on streaming platforms, offering something for every kind of viewer. This week, we're diving into **Rose of Nevada**, a captivating time-travel mystery, and **The Sun Never Sets**, an emotionally charged love triangle drama starring **Dakota Fanning** and **Jake Johnson**.

**Rose of Nevada** whisks us away to a remote fishing village where a decades-lost ship, the titular **Rose of Nevada**, has mysteriously reappeared. Its return is seen as a beacon of hope for the struggling community, sparking dreams of renewed prosperity. Joining the crew are **Nick** (played by **George MacKay**), a man desperate to provide for his family, and **Liam** (played by **Callum Turner**), a drifter seeking to outrun his past. Their voyage aboard the resurrected vessel becomes a journey not just through the ocean, but through time itself, as they find themselves transported to the past.

Meanwhile, **The Sun Never Sets** explores the complexities of modern relationships. **Wendy** (Fanning), living in Alaska, finds her world turned upside down when her older, divorced boyfriend, **Jack** (Johnson), asks for space to re-evaluate their relationship. During their time apart, Wendy reconnects with her ex, **Chuck** (played by **Cory Michael Smith**). This reunion ignites a potent love triangle, forcing all three characters to confront difficult truths about love, timing, and the messy process of personal growth.

## A Voyage Through Time and Emotion

These new arrivals cater to fans eager for narratives that blend suspense with heartfelt drama. **Rose of Nevada** promises a unique blend of historical mystery and science fiction, leaning into the allure of the unknown and the promise of second chances. The concept of a ship reappearing after decades, especially one tied to a community's fortunes, is ripe for exploration, hinting at deeper secrets than just a simple return.

On the other hand, **The Sun Never Sets** delves into the intimate landscape of human connection. The film's focus on a love triangle, particularly one involving characters at different stages of life and emotional baggage, suggests a nuanced exploration of commitment and self-discovery. The chemistry between **Fanning**, **Johnson**, and **Smith** will undoubtedly be key to navigating these complex emotional currents, offering a relatable, albeit dramatic, look at relationships.

## What Fans Are Waiting For

For fans of genre-bending stories, **Rose of Nevada** offers a fresh take on time travel, moving away from typical sci-fi tropes into something more atmospheric and perhaps even elegiac. The casting of **George MacKay**, known for his intense performances, alongside the enigmatic **Callum Turner**, builds anticipation for a story rich in character and intrigue. Likewise, enthusiasts of character-driven dramas will be drawn to **The Sun Never Sets**, eager to see how **Dakota Fanning** and **Jake Johnson** navigate the emotional fallout of a rekindled romance and an uncertain future.

## What's Next

While specific streaming availability details beyond their arrival on platforms are still emerging for some titles, the immediate availability of **Rose of Nevada** and **The Sun Never Sets** means audiences can start exploring these compelling narratives right away. Keep an eye out for further details on other titles mentioned in this week's streaming drop.

How many books have been written, how many movies made about the outlaw? With  The Death of Robin Hood , writer-director Michael Sarnoski goes back to the source. Rather, the  supposed  sources. The earliest stories of Robin Hood were ballads told by commoners across England. These tales tell of an outlaw who does not give anything stolen to the poor, instead taking pleasure in killing the rich. In the medieval ballad “Robin Hood and Guy of Gisborne,” Robin beheads Gisborne and sticks his head on a spike. – Dan M. ( full review ) Where to Stream: HBO Max Hanging by a Wire (Mohammed Ali Naqvi) A brisk docu-thriller that could do more with the richness of the players it chronicles, Mohammed Ali Naqvi’s Hanging by a Wire is not without thrills and human drama. Yet it seems focused more on a death-defying rescue than on what could be done to prevent this from happening again. – John F. ( full review ) Where to Stream: VOD Hope (Na Hong-jin) It’s never night in Hope Harbor. At least so long as we’re there. The eschatological events of writer-director Na Hong-Jin’s high-octane, highly anticipated Hope unfold over the course of one long, grueling, nonstop chase of a day for its rag-tag team of small-town South Korean cops, yokels, and hicks, an ensemble that ranges from heroic to hilarious in this blathering creature-feature phantasm. – Luke H. ( full review ) Where to Stream: VOD In the Mouth (Cory Santilli) One of the most impressive American indies I’ve seen in the last year sets Free Time and Dad & Step-Dad star Colin Burgess in a surreal comedy. Cory Santilli’s In the Mouth premiered at the Slamdance Film Festival and has now arrived digitally. Where to Stream: Fandor Rose of Nevada (Mark Jenkin) The films of Mark Jenkin ooze a hypnotic, seasick sensibility; to watch them is to be lulled by their restless jumps through time and space, their ability to convert his home turf of Cornwall into a suspended world where facts and visions collide in stupefying dioramas. The director is a spinner of wandering tales, never fueled by linear plots so much as ambient forces: a ticking clock, gusts of wind, the distant roaring of waves. His dramas tend to pull your gaze from people and toward the inanimate objects that litter their surroundings.
